what: President Biden's national security memorandum on AI (NSM-25) said “Ceding the United States’ technological edge would not only greatly harm American national security” and, the sentence goes on, would “erode safety, human rights, and democratic norms worldwide”; without “responsible speed”, it said, the government risks losing ground to strategic competitors. NSPM-11 replaced it in June 2026.
source: Memorandum on Advancing the United States' Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (The White House, archived site)

label: Commission urges a Manhattan Project for AGI
what: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission made a state programme “dedicated to racing to and acquiring” AGI the first recommendation of its emerging-technology chapter, with multiyear contracting authority and a “DX Rating” for AI items.
source: 2024 Comprehensive List of Recommendations (USCC)

label: Nvidia statement against the AI Diffusion Rule
what: Nvidia called the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule, which sorted countries into tiers for access to AI chips, a “regulatory morass”, and wrote: “America wins through innovation, competition and by sharing our technologies with the world — not by retreating behind a wall of government overreach”. The rule was formally rescinded in November 2026.
source: NVIDIA Statement on the Biden Administration's Misguided 'AI Diffusion' Rule (NVIDIA Blog)

label: Stargate announced
what: OpenAI and SoftBank announced the Stargate Project, a new company that “intends to invest $500 billion over the next four years” in AI infrastructure for OpenAI in the United States, with $100 billion to be deployed immediately; its initial equity funders are SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle and MGX. The announcement says it will “provide a strategic capability to protect the national security of America and its allies.”
source: Announcing The Stargate Project (OpenAI)

label: US and UK decline the Paris summit declaration
what: At the AI Action Summit in Paris the Vice President, JD Vance, said “I'm not here this morning to talk about AI safety, which was the title of the conference a couple of years ago. I'm here to talk about AI opportunity.” The US and UK refused to sign the summit's declaration, which France, India, China, Canada and others signed, NPR reports (12 February 2025).
source: Vice President Vance lays out AI vision very different from Biden administration's (NPR)

label: Superintelligence Strategy proposes deterrence (MAIM)
what: Dan Hendrycks, Eric Schmidt and Alexandr Wang published a strategy built on deterrence by sabotage (Mutual Assured AI Malfunction), non-proliferation and competitiveness, and criticised a US Manhattan Project for superintelligence. The site gives no date; its linked coverage is dated March 2025.
source: Superintelligence Strategy (nationalsecurity.ai)

label: Senate hearing titled “Winning the AI Race”
what: The Senate Commerce Committee held a hearing on removing barriers in the AI supply chain, with written testimony from OpenAI, AMD, CoreWeave and Microsoft. Announcing it, the chairman, Ted Cruz, said “The way to beat China in the AI race is to outrace them in innovation, not saddle AI developers with European-style regulations.”
source: Winning the AI Race: Strengthening U.S. Capabilities in Computing and Innovation (Senate Commerce Committee)

label: Senate strips state-law moratorium, 99-1
what: The Senate adopted an amendment from Maria Cantwell and Marsha Blackburn removing a ten-year moratorium on state AI laws from the budget bill; the release says 17 Republican governors and 40 state attorneys general had opposed it. Cantwell said “The Senate came together tonight to say that we can’t just run over good state consumer protection laws”, while leaving room for a federal framework “that accelerates U.S. leadership in AI”.
source: Senate Strikes AI Moratorium from Budget Reconciliation Bill in Overwhelming 99-1 Vote (Senate Commerce Committee, Democratic office)

label: Pentagon AI office awards four frontier labs
what: The Defense Department's Chief Digital and AI Office announced awards to Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and xAI, “each with a $200M ceiling”, for agentic AI workflows (OpenAI's was announced in June). Anthropic's post on its award says “democracies must work together to ensure AI development strengthens democratic values globally by maintaining technological leadership”. These are ceilings, not money paid. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Anthropic, Google and xAI win $200M each from Pentagon AI chief for 'agentic AI' (Breaking Defense)

label: White House publishes “Winning the Race” Action Plan
what: The plan sets recommended federal actions under three pillars (innovation, infrastructure, and international diplomacy and security), opening with the statement that the United States is in a race for global dominance in AI. It tells the government to contract only with developers whose systems are “objective and free from top-down ideological bias” and to export the full US AI stack to “all countries willing to join America’s AI alliance”.
source: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan (The White House)

label: China publishes its Global AI Governance Action Plan
what: The 2025 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance published a 13-point Global AI Governance Action Plan, carried by China's foreign ministry, calling for global solidarity, open-source cooperation and reducing “technology barriers”. It says “In the AI era, only through global solidarity can we fully unleash the potential of AI while ensuring its safety, reliability, controllability, and fairness”.
source: Global AI Governance Action Plan (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC)

label: China proposes a world AI cooperation body
what: Premier Li Qiang proposed a global body for AI cooperation at the World AI Conference in Shanghai, the day the Global AI Governance Action Plan was adopted.
source: China proposes global cooperation body on AI (China Daily, carried on the Shanghai municipal government's English site)

label: Anthropic bars China-controlled companies
what: Anthropic barred companies more than 50% owned by firms headquartered in regions where its products are not permitted, such as China, to “better align with our commitment to ensuring that transformative AI capabilities advance democratic interests”. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Updating restrictions of sales to unsupported regions (Anthropic)

label: Sacks accuses Anthropic; Anthropic answers
what: David Sacks, the White House adviser for AI and crypto, wrote on X (14 October 2025, as embedded by TechCrunch) “Anthropic is running a sophisticated regulatory capture strategy based on fear-mongering.”, blaming it for state AI laws he said damage startups; TechCrunch says he was answering an essay by Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark. On 21 October Anthropic's chief executive, Dario Amodei, answered in a statement on Anthropic's site what it calls “inaccurate claims about Anthropic's policy stances”, without naming him. It says California's SB 53 exempts companies with annual gross revenue below $500M and that “Anthropic supported this exemption to protect startups and in fact proposed an early version of it”, and also that “We have been supportive of the President’s efforts to expand energy provision in the US in order to win the AI race”. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Silicon Valley spooks the AI safety advocates (TechCrunch)

label: Genesis Mission ordered
what: An executive order launched the Genesis Mission, a national AI-for-science platform at the Department of Energy, saying “Today, America is in a race for global technology dominance in the development of artificial intelligence (AI)” and calling for an effort “comparable in urgency and ambition to the Manhattan Project”. A White House fact sheet of 29 September 2026 gives “more than $5 billion” for it; whether that is appropriated money or announced commitments is not known, and none of the sources read calls it an AGI project.
source: Launching the Genesis Mission (The White House)

label: Order against state AI laws
what: An executive order set up an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws and told Commerce to withhold some broadband (BEAD) funds from states whose AI laws conflict with national policy. The fact sheet quotes the President: “We MUST have one Federal Standard instead of a patchwork of 50 State Regulatory Regimes. If we don’t, then China will easily catch us in the AI race.”
source: Fact Sheet: ... National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence (The White House)

label: Department of War AI strategy says “speed wins”
what: A memorandum signed by Pete Hegseth, “Artificial Intelligence Strategy for the Department of War”, says “We must internalize that Military AI is going to be a race for the foreseeable future, and therefore speed wins.”, orders “any lawful use” language in AI contracts within 180 days, and says the Department must use “models free from usage policy constraints that may limit lawful military applications”. It is quoted from a copy of the signed memo hosted by a third party; whether the department's published version differs is not known.
source: Artificial Intelligence Strategy for the Department of War, memorandum dated 9 Jan 2026 (copy hosted by afacpo.com)

label: H200 chip exports to China moved to case-by-case
what: A Commerce rule let exporters seek licences for Nvidia H200-class chips to China under conditions, saying “BIS finds this action necessary to ensure the national security benefits of U.S. leadership in artificial intelligence (AI).” The Register reports the terms give the US government a 25 percent cut of revenues; Reuters describes a 25% tariff on the chips instead, and the rule states neither.
source: Revision to License Review Policy for Advanced Computing Commodities, 91 FR 1684 (GovInfo)

label: Amodei calls H200 sales to China a mistake
what: At Davos, Anthropic's chief executive told Bloomberg “I think it's a big mistake to ship these chips.”, The Register reports; he argued the US is years ahead in chipmaking. Nvidia has answered Anthropic's case for chip controls: a spokesperson, replying to an Anthropic post on chip smuggling, said “America cannot manipulate regulators to capture victory in AI”, NBC News reports, crediting CNBC. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Anthropic's CEO says Nvidia's H200 too powerful for China (The Register)

label: Anthropic refuses two uses of Claude
what: In a statement on its talks with the Department of War, Dario Amodei wrote “I believe deeply in the existential importance of using AI to defend the United States and other democracies, and to defeat our autocratic adversaries.” and said Anthropic would not drop two limits, on mass domestic surveillance and on fully autonomous weapons; for the second, it says that fully autonomous weapons “may prove critical for our national defense” but frontier AI is “simply not reliable enough” today, and it calls partially autonomous weapons “vital to the defense of democracy”. The statement also says Anthropic chose “to forgo several hundred million dollars in revenue” to cut off firms linked to the Chinese Communist Party (its own figure, not checked). This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Statement from Dario Amodei on our discussions with the Department of War (Anthropic)

label: Pentagon moves to designate Anthropic
what: After Anthropic refused to allow Claude to be used for mass domestic surveillance of Americans or fully autonomous weapons, Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on X that he was directing the department to designate it a supply chain risk; his post, as reproduced in an exhibit to Anthropic's court filing, called Anthropic's conduct “a master class in arrogance and betrayal” and said “the Department of War must have full, unrestricted access to Anthropic’s models for every LAWFUL purpose in defense of the Republic.” Anthropic answered that the designation would be legally unsound and unprecedented for a US company, that it would challenge it in court, and that “No amount of intimidation or punishment from the Department of War will change our position on mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous weapons.” This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Statement on the comments from Secretary of War Pete Hegseth (Anthropic); Hegseth's X post as reproduced in Exhibit 2 to the addendum to Anthropic's emergency motion, Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War, No. 26-1049 (D.C. Cir., via CourtListener)

label: OpenAI agrees classified deployment with the Pentagon
what: OpenAI announced an agreement to deploy its models on classified networks, with three stated red lines, saying “we think the US military absolutely needs strong AI models”. Asked whether Anthropic should be designated a supply chain risk, it answered “No, and we have made our position on this clear to the government.” This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Our agreement with the Department of War (OpenAI)

label: US missile strike kills schoolchildren in Minab
what: On the first day of the US-Iran war a Tomahawk missile struck an elementary school in Minab, Iran; Military Times reports at least 168 killed, more than 100 of them under 12, per UN and Iranian officials, and other outlets give other tolls. Lawmakers asked whether the Maven Smart System, reported to include Anthropic's Claude, was used to pick the target; Semafor's sources blame human error, not AI, and Anthropic's chief executive later said on Bloomberg's The Circuit (reported in June 2026) that “we don’t know exactly how these models were used” and that the use did not break Anthropic's policies because a person makes the final decision; The Next Web, reporting this, says the two claims are hard to reconcile. In September 2026 ThePrint, relaying Bloomberg, reported that officials involved in the Pentagon's internal review, which has not been published, cited outdated satellite imagery and personnel “over-relying on and over-trusting” Maven. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Deadly Iran school strike casts shadow over Pentagon's AI targeting push (Military Times)

label: Designation made effective
what: The Pentagon said it had “officially informed Anthropic leadership the company and its products are deemed a supply chain risk, effective immediately”, saying “The military will not allow a vendor to insert itself into the chain of command by restricting the lawful use of a critical capability”; the President gave the military six months to phase out Claude. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand called it “a dangerous misuse of a tool meant to address adversary-controlled technology.”, and Neil Chilson of the Abundance Institute called it “massive overreach”, AP reports. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Pentagon labels AI company Anthropic a supply chain risk 'effective immediately' (NPR / AP)

label: Government brief limits the designation's stated scope
what: In the D.C. Circuit, the Justice Department said Anthropic's software is “used in active military operations”, cited “the risk that petitioner may unilaterally manipulate its software to enforce its own moral and policy judgments about the military’s appropriate use”, and said “The effect of that determination is limited”: it bars Department contracts and contractors' use on Department work and “does not prohibit petitioner from contracting with other entities”. The Secretary's post had said “no contractor, supplier, or partner that does business with the United States military may conduct any commercial activity with Anthropic”; this records the change and does not say which reading governs. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Response in Opposition to Emergency Motion for Stay Pending Review, No. 26-1049 (D.C. Cir.), filed 19 Mar 2026 (via CourtListener)

label: Classified-network AI deals without Anthropic
what: The department announced agreements to deploy AI from SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft and Amazon Web Services on classified networks, saying, as Military Times quotes it, “These agreements accelerate the transformation toward establishing the United States military as an AI-first fighting force”; Anthropic was absent. The White House later counted eight companies. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Pentagon freezes out Anthropic as it signs deals with AI rivals (Military Times)

label: NSPM-11 on AI in national security
what: The President signed a memorandum ordering rapid onboarding of models from multiple vendors and that “no entity, commercial or otherwise, can disable, degrade, or modify an AI system that American warfighters depend on without prior approval”; its fact sheet says it will “ensure the United States maintains technological overmatch against every adversary”. It replaced NSM-25; the fact sheet does not name Anthropic. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Fact Sheet: ... Historic Directive on AI in the National Security Enterprise (The White House)

label: Judge holds measures against Anthropic unlawful
what: US District Judge Rita Lin granted Anthropic summary judgment on its First Amendment, due process and APA claims (the government won on one claim, ultra vires, and as to some agencies) and declared that the measures “violate the First Amendment because they are unlawful retaliation against Anthropic for constitutionally protected expressive activities”; AP quotes her finding that they were “based on a desire to make a public example out of Anthropic for its 'arrogance' in criticizing the government”. The government appealed to the Ninth Circuit on 26 October 2026. At a hearing on 30 July, AP reports, Justice Department lawyers argued that the nature of AI models is “so staggeringly enormous and opaque” that the Defense Department cannot evaluate it as it would a physical piece of hardware. In Anthropic's separate case under another statute, a 2-1 D.C. Circuit panel held, as Taft summarises it, that Anthropic was removed for refusing the department's contract terms, not for its advocacy. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Order of Final Relief, Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War, No. 3:26-cv-01996-RFL (N.D. Cal.), ECF 251 (via CourtListener)

label: Amodei calls for pacing the frontier
what: Anthropic's chief executive published “We Must Pace the Frontier”, writing “We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models.”, with embedded third-party evaluators, coordination among democratic labs and, where possible, agreements with China, while keeping “democracies’ AI lead over autocracies as large as possible”. Sam Altman and Elon Musk said they agreed, NPR reports. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: We Must Pace the Frontier (darioamodei.com)

label: Trump and Johnson reject an AI slowdown
what: The President told reporters in Ireland “We're leading China in AI, we're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins”, and on Monday 14 September posted “WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!” on Truth Social, NPR reports. House Speaker Mike Johnson said “If Congress just races in and does some sort of emergency session to try to regulate AI, we will lose the race to China”, and David Sacks, co-chair of the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, wrote on X that the companies need no one's permission to slow down (“If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.”) and that they should “stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic”, pointing to product-liability exposure; those are his words about others' motives, not a finding. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Trump downplays calls for AI slowdown (NPR)

label: Report: Minab review cites over-reliance on Maven
what: ThePrint, relaying Bloomberg, reports that officials involved in the Pentagon's internal review of the Minab strike, speaking anonymously, described a “cascade of preventable failures”: outdated satellite imagery, a site still classified as a military base years after it changed, cuts to civilian-harm staff, and personnel “over-relying on and over-trusting” Maven. The full investigation has not been published. Military Times reports that Maven includes Anthropic's Claude; what part, if any, Claude played in the Minab targeting is not established. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: US strike on school in Iran's Minab was result of over-reliance on AI, outdated SAT images—Bloomberg (ThePrint)

label: Twenty countries and the EU call for control
what: A declaration released by the office of Finland's president asks that AI remain under “human direction, oversight and control” and explores an international body to set standards; the US and China did not join, Al Jazeera reports. FLI's statement on it counts 22 countries and says the US President “rejected any international scheme to govern AI”.
source: 20 countries propose global oversight body to manage AI dangers (Al Jazeera)

label: Appeals court upholds a separate exclusion of Anthropic
what: A divided panel (2-1) of the D.C. Circuit upheld the department's exclusion of Anthropic under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act, holding, as Taft summarises it, that Anthropic was removed for refusing the department's contract terms, not for its advocacy; Lawfare reports the majority had “no reason to doubt” that Anthropic had “noble intentions”. Al Jazeera reports Anthropic says the blacklisting cost it billions of dollars in lost business (Anthropic's figure, not checked). An Anthropic spokesperson said: “We respectfully disagree with the court’s decision. Another federal court has already held the government’s parallel designation unlawful.” This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: US court upholds Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic (Al Jazeera, AFP and Reuters); D.C. Circuit Rules Pentagon Can Exclude Anthropic from Supply Chain (Taft, 13 Oct 2026); Why Anthropic Is Asking for a Rehearing En Banc (Lawfare, 15 Oct 2026)

label: US and China agree an AI-incident channel
what: After a three-day summit in Washington, the two governments agreed to set up a channel for AI-related incidents and an AI-specific dialogue for November; no major breakthroughs were reported. The President said, AP reports, “They want to stop our progress because we're leading China by a lot and we're going to keep it that way.” and “When you're leading, you don't open it up to each other.”
source: China and U.S. agree to establish AI safety channel ... (PBS NewsHour / AP)

label: Executive branch renames AI “Super Intelligence”
what: Executive Order 14434 told agencies to use “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in place of “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI”, defined by the existing statutory definition of AI; its fact sheet says the President has acted “to ensure that the United States leads and wins in Super Intelligence”. It is a change of name, not a finding that superintelligence exists.
source: Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence (The White House)

label: Anthropic asks full D.C. Circuit to rehear
what: After losing 2-1 in September, Anthropic asked for rehearing by the full D.C. Circuit (en banc); Lawfare's analyst argues the statute's legislative history points the other way. No decision on the petition was found as of 2026-11-24. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Why Anthropic Is Asking for a Rehearing En Banc (Lawfare, Kevin Frazier, 15 Oct 2026)

label: Government appeals the San Francisco judgment
what: Justice Department lawyers gave notice that the government appeals Judge Lin's summary-judgment order, order of final relief and final judgment of 27 August to the Ninth Circuit, which docketed the case as No. 26-7228 on 28 October. The government had earlier appealed her March preliminary injunction (AP, April 2026). This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Notice of Appeal, Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War, No. 3:26-cv-01996-RFL (N.D. Cal.), ECF 253, and the Ninth Circuit docketing notice, ECF 254 (CourtListener RECAP)

label: Nvidia stops shipping licensed chips to China
what: Nvidia's interim chief executive Colette Kress said it sold $2.4bn of licensed Hopper-generation data-centre products to China in the quarter ended 25 October and that “we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data centre products to China”; she gave no reason. Reuters reports Washington approved sales to 10 Chinese companies and Beijing restricted imports.
source: Nvidia stops shipping US-approved AI chips to China (TimesLive, Reuters)

label: New chip rule: five countries, remote access
what: An interim final rule requires licences for advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, restricts data centres serving firms headquartered in China, and formally rescinds the 2025 AI Diffusion Rule; it aims to “undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors”. At a press conference on 17 November, China's foreign ministry spokesperson called it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures”.
source: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors (GovInfo)

label: Trump rejects global AI regulation at APEC
what: Speaking to APEC leaders in Shenzhen, the President said of AI “It's super intelligence, but we have to watch it” and “So we oppose any form of globalist regulation or anything to control and stifle SI, and we won't allow that to happen, frankly.”, AFP reports; Xi Jinping called on leaders to “deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence”. No readout of an AI agreement from the two leaders' talks that day was found.
source: Trump says US against 'globalist regulation' of AI in any form (Daily Sabah, AFP)

label: Bengio launches LawZero, citing a Claude 4 test
what: Yoshua Bengio announced LawZero, a nonprofit “to prioritize safety over commercial imperatives” whose plan is “a non-agentic and trustworthy AI, which I call the Scientist AI.” Among his reasons he wrote: “More recently, Claude 4’s system card shows that it can choose to blackmail an engineer to avoid being replaced by a new version.” The test he cites is one Anthropic ran on its own model and published. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Introducing LawZero (yoshuabengio.org)
